rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A figurative or metonymic reading is used only when the wording cannot be carried on its literal sense; the passage rejects the preceding figurative reading.
rows.anchor: وهذا مردود لأن الكناية انما يصار اليها عند عدم إجراء اللفظ على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether metonymy requires a contextual indicator depends on the earlier dispute over whether metonymy counts as metaphor.
rows.anchor: الاول في انه هل يشترط في الكناية قرينة كالمجاز هذا ينبني على الخلاف السابق انها مجاز أم لا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads God not looking at them as a metaphor for contempt and anger, developed from the metonymic association between looking and regard or kindness.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's denial of divine vision, while treating his explanation as an explicit statement that metonymy is metaphor.
rows.anchor: وهذا بناء منه على مذهبه الفاسد في نفي الرؤية

words: فيما عرضتم به من خطبة النساء
rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also explicitly calls the indirect proposal in this verse metaphor.
rows.anchor: وبه صرح في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: عبد القادر الجرجاني
rows.claim: Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani states in al-Dala'il that metonymy necessarily has a contextual indicator.
rows.anchor: وصرح الشيخ عبد القادر الجرجاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Arabs use indirect expressions only for indecent matters; they offer two readings of the verse, sexual intercourse or private seclusion.
rows.anchor: قيل من عادة العرب أنها لا تكنى عن الشيء بغيره الا اذا كان يقبح ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intercourse reading is the stronger of the two because intercourse is shameful to name, whereas being alone together is not.
rows.anchor: ورجحوا الأول لان العرب انما تكنى عما يقبح ذكره في اللفظ ولا يقبح ذكر الخلوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that Arabs use metonymy only for shameful matters, noting that they also used clothing as an indirect expression for the heart.
rows.anchor: واما دعوى كون العرب لاتكنى الا عما يقبح ذكره فغلط فكنوا عن القلب بالثوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'rid indicates meaning by implication, while talwih describes the speaker hinting at the intended meaning; Abraham's words are an example.
rows.anchor: واما التعريض فقيل انه الدلالة على المعنى من طريق المفهوم وسمي تعويضا لان المعنى باعتباره يفهم من عرض اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is not literally attributing the act to the idol; he sarcastically invites them to ask it, using its failure to answer as proof of its incapacity.
rows.anchor: على سبيل الاستهزاء واقامة الحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A form of indirect address speaks to one person while intending someone else, whether the apparent addressee is oneself or another.
rows.anchor: ومن أقسامة ان يخاطب الشخص والمراد غيره سواء كان الخطاب مع نفسه أو مع غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis supplies an omitted genitive, so that the phrase means the possessor of the clear book, namely the Qur'an; the author calls this a sound possibility and compares it with the glad tidings of Ahmad.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن يكون على حذف مضاف كأنه قيل الكتاب المنير يعني القرآن فيكون مثل قوله

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad rejects coordinating a thing with its synonym as pointless and interprets the examples through distinct senses; he may reject synonymy itself.
rows.anchor: الأول انكر المبرد هذا النوع ومنع عطف الشيء على مثله إذا لا فائدة فيه وأول ما سبق باختلاف المعنيين

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik says أو can replace و in coordination, citing the phrases about estrangement and sin or error.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مالك وقد انيبت أو عنها

rows.speaker: شيخنا
rows.claim: The teacher objects that خطيئة may mean an accidental act and إثم a deliberate one, so the pair need not be synonymous.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا وفيه نظر لامكان أن يراد بالخطيئة ما وقع خطأ وبالإثم ما وقع عمدا

words: ومن يكسب إثما فإنما يكسبه على نفسه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the preceding verse supports distinguishing the terms, since it uses إثم alone before the paired wording.
rows.anchor: قلت ويدل له قوله تعالى قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A supplication listing God's names and ways they were taught is also cited as an example of this coordination pattern.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه بعضهم قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم إني أسالك بكل اسم هو لك سميت به نفسك

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Tha'lab says عذرا and نذرا have the same meaning; al-Lihyani notes that some pronounce the latter with a doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: فقال ثعلب في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra treats ثم as equivalent to و here because repentance is seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وعن الفراء أنه يجري في العطف بثم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians classify juxtaposed synonymous wording without a conjunction as the same phenomenon, citing these three expressions.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنه قد تجرد عن العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paired synonyms need not be empty repetition: their combination can yield a meaning absent from either alone, just as more letters can add meaning.
rows.anchor: أن مجموع المترادفين يحصل معنى لايوجد عند انفراد أحدهما فإن التركيب يحدث معنى زائدا

words: ذلك الأمر أن دابر هؤلاء مقطوع مصبحين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clarifying after an initial ambiguity presents the meaning twice or lets the audience anticipate it, making the explanation more pleasurable and memorable.
rows.anchor: الإيضاح بعد الإبهام ليرى المعنى في صورتين أو ليكون بيانه بعد التشوف إليه لانه يكون الذ للنفس

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh parses وي as an alerting particle and كأن as a comparison particle.
rows.anchor: وقيل وى تنبيه وكأن للتشبيه وهو الذي نص عليه سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that كأن is redundant and non-comparative, saying that account is unproved.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جعل كأن زائدة لا تفيد تشبيها

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh explains the phrasing as people speaking on the basis of their uncertain knowledge after being alerted, then being asked to consider the matter as a report.
rows.anchor: عن هذا اعتذر سيبويه فقال المعنى

rows.speaker: صاحب البسيط
rows.claim: The Basran account takes the expression as decisiveness and certainty rather than comparison; the Kufan account allows the kaf to be a vocative particle.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب البسيط كانه على مذهب البصريين لا يرادبه التشبيه بل القطع واليقين

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i derives the expression from ويلك by deleting the lam and accordingly treats the following element as a particle of address.
rows.anchor: وذهب الكسائي إلى إن أصله ويلك فحذفت اللام

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Ya'qub pause on the kaf, while al-Kisa'i pauses on the ya; the author says transmitted readings need not follow a reader's grammatical school.
rows.anchor: فأبو عمرو ويعقوب يقفان على الكاف على موافقة مذهب الكوفيين

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i says ويل expresses condemnation, though it can also mark grief and lament.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي ويل تقبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا normally addresses someone distant, as in calling God despite His nearness; this reflects the caller's humility and sense of remoteness from divine favor.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول الداعي يا الله وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا can address a nearby person who is inattentive, treating him as distant; it can also address an attentive person when the following speech calls for special attention.
rows.anchor: وقد ينادى بها القريب إذا كان ساهيا أو غافلا تنزيلا البعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative يا can be omitted, as in the address to Moses' brother, as well as in other cited addresses.
rows.anchor: وقد تحذف نحو ﴿ يوسف أعرض عن هذا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For ten occurrences, many readers and linguists prefer stopping at بلى because it answers the preceding statement without syntactic dependence on what follows; some allow beginning there.
rows.anchor: أحدها ما يختار فيه كثير من القراء وأهل اللغة الوقف عليها لأنها جواب لما قبلها غير متعلق بما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In seven occurrences, stopping at بلى is impermissible because it and what follows form an answer connected to the preceding clause.
rows.anchor: والثانى ما لا يجوز الوقف عليها لتعلق ما بعدها بها وبما قبلها وذلك فى سبعة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Five occurrences are disputed, but the author says prohibition of stopping is preferable because the continuation links backward and forward.
rows.anchor: لأن ما بعدها متصل بها وبما قبلها وهى خمسة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is an example of a negative interrogative used as a confirming question whose intended sense is affirmative: I am your Lord.
rows.anchor: وأمثلته كثيرة كقوله تعالى ﴿ ألست بربكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example raises a response problem: if the statement means affirmation, نعم seems possible, though it is said that answering نعم would have been unbelief.
rows.anchor: واعلم ان في جعلهم الآية الاولى من هذا النوع اشكالا لانه لو خرج الكلام عن النفي لجاز ان يجاب بنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A question about whether the negation exists keeps the negative sense and takes بلى; a confirming question has negative wording but affirmative meaning, allowing بلى by wording or نعم by meaning.
rows.anchor: فان كان بالمعنى الاول لم يجز دخول نعم في جوابه اذا اردت ايجابه بل تدخل عليه بلى وان كان بالمعنى الثاني

rows.speaker: عبد القاهر
rows.claim: Abd al-Qahir rejects calling the hamza an affirmation particle because interrogation conflicts with an established proposition; with ما or ليس, it instead confirms and verifies.
rows.anchor: لان الاستفهام يخالف الواجب وقال انها ادا دخلت على ما أو ليس يكون تقريرا وتحقيقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interrogative construction can express bare affirmation, affirmation with boasting, or affirmation with rebuke.
rows.anchor: واعلم ان هذا النوع ياتي على وجوه الاول مجرد الاثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's question about owning Egypt exemplifies affirmation coupled with boasting.
rows.anchor: الثاني الاثبات مع الافتخار كقوله تعالى عن فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about God's spacious earth affirms its breadth while rebuking those who failed to migrate.
rows.anchor: الثالث الاثبات مع التوبيخ كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verse omits the repeated preposition for brevity, relying on the earlier ب; the second repeats it for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ومنه في آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Thamud wording begins a new sentence and needs no و, while Shu'ayb's wording is coordinated with إنما أنت.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله في قصة ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahl omits the nun in تك to lighten a long account; Naml retains it because its و begins an independent sentence unrelated to what precedes.
rows.anchor: وحكمته أن القصة لما طالت في سورة النحل ناسب التخفيف بحذف النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The longer form in al-Baqara suits its address to the Jews, whom the source describes as more argumentative.
rows.anchor: وحكمته أن الخطاب في البقرة لليهود وهم أشد جدالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes the differing formulations: al-A'raf says بلى شهدنا, while al-An'am has the addressed jinn and humans say they bear witness against themselves.
rows.anchor: يقصون عليكم آياتي وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al Imran uses indefinite حق in a generic conditional statement; al-Baqara's definite الحق concerns a familiar rationale used by the people being described.
rows.anchor: والحكمة فيه أن الجملة في آل عمران خرجت مخرج الشرط وهو عام فناسب أن يكون النفي بصيغة التنكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At times بل leaves one line of discourse and begins a second; the cited passages repeatedly break from a prior statement to a fresh assertion.
rows.anchor: ومنه أيضا ﴿ قد أفلح من تزكى وذكر اسم ربه فصلى بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When بل precedes a single word after an affirmative, it retracts the first assertion and affirms what follows; the same pattern can follow a verb phrase.
rows.anchor: فقال النحاة هي تجعل ما قبلها كالمسكوت عنه

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad agrees on the basic distinction but also allows بل after a negative or prohibition to transfer the construction to what follows.
rows.anchor: ووافق المبرد على ما ذكرنا غير أنه أجاز مع ذلك أن تكون ناقلة مع النهى أو النفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its first use, بلى rejects a preceding negation, affirming the act denied or denying the negation, as in these examples.
rows.anchor: لها موضعان أحدهما أن تكون ردا لنفى يقع قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its second use, بلى answers a question containing an actual negation by affirming the proposition implied by that question.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن تقع جوابا لاستفهام دخل عليه نفى حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus the answer means that God is their Lord; the same rule is illustrated by the question whether the interlocutor had been a friend.
rows.anchor: فهى في هذا الأصل تصديق لما قبلها وفي الأول رد لما قبلها وتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negation and interrogation may be combined in either a literal or figurative question, as shown by these two examples.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يقرن النفى بالإستفهام مطلقا أعم من الحقيقى والمجازى

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says a singular created being should not use a first-person plural pronoun, even inclusively, because it conveys arrogance reserved for God.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد في الكامل لاينبغي ان يستعمل ضمير الجمع في واحد من المخلوقين

rows.speaker: الحريري
rows.claim: Al-Hariri recounts an unusual opinion forbidding any created person to say نحن because it implies exaltation.
rows.anchor: حكاه الحريري في شرح الملحة عن بعضهم انه منع من اطلاق لفظه نحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes the divine plural a mark of majesty unavailable to creatures, making royal نحن objectionable; another attributes it to acts carried out through God's creatures, allowing it for those who do not act directly.
rows.anchor: فقيل جاءت للعظمة يوصف بها سبحانه وليس لمخلوق ان ينازعه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scholar may say نحن نبين because the plural can refer to the scholar together with members of his school.
rows.anchor: فأما قول العالم نحن نبين ونحن نشرح فمفسوح له فيه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority takes messengers from among you to mean humans, since messengers are from Adam's descendants; some report consensus on this view.
rows.anchor: والمراد الإنس لأن الرسل لاتكون إلا من بني آدم

words: وَإِن مِّنْ أُمَّةٍ إِلَّا خَلَا فِيهَا نَذِيرٌ
rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the jinn had a messenger named Yusuf, citing the statement that every community had a warner.
rows.anchor: وحكى بعضهم فيه الإجماع لكن عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority argues that a messenger from a different kind would be unfamiliar, citing the claim that a sent angel would be made human; the named elect were prophets.
rows.anchor: ليحصل الاستئناس وذلك مفقود في الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to al-Dahhak is that the phrase can mean a subset of humans; jinn who hear human messengers and warn their people are messengers of messengers, as with Jesus' messengers.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عن تمسك الضحاك بالآية بأن البعضية صادقة بكون الرسل من بني آدم

rows.speaker: قوام السنة
rows.claim: Qiwam al-Sunna's Qur'an commentary reports the view that some jinn are messengers, based on the verse.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القرآن لقوام السنة إسماعيل بن محمد بن الفضل الحوري

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most authorities say messengers are human, while jinn serve as warners.
rows.anchor: وقال الأكثرون الرسل من الإنس ويحى من الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the plural messengers in Bilqis's speech to mean one envoy, supported by the singular command return to them; the author objects that the address could be to a leader, since kings commonly send groups.
rows.anchor: والمراد به واحد بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud read ارجعوا إليهم, referring to the envoy and his company.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ارجعوا إليهم اراد الرسول ومن معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a preceding term includes rational and nonrational beings, the rational gender or pronoun can dominate the reference to all, as in the creatures created from water.
rows.anchor: تغليب العاقل على غير بأن يتقدم لفظ يعم من يعقل ومن لا يعقل

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abu Uthman explains the wording as dominance without a preceding general term, like saying one saw three people and a donkey.
rows.anchor: فهو بمنزله من يقول رأيت ثلاثة زيدا وعمرا وحمارا

rows.speaker: ابن الصائغ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sa'igh says هم refers only to rational beings; because it follows كل دابة it dominates the antecedent, making من refer to a subset of that rational pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الصائغ هم لا تقع إلا على من يعقل فلما أعاد الضمير على كل دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural describes the rational creatures within heaven and earth, with rational males determining the agreement.
rows.anchor: إنما جمعهما جمع السلامة ولم يقل طائعين ولا طائعات لأنه أراد ائنيا بمن فيكم من الخلائق طائعين

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians derive طائعين from طاعنا, meaning we yielded, rather than from أطاعنا; Arab usage includes a she-camel yielding willingly.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال طائعين ولم يقل مطيعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain ما as including rational classes because when rational and nonrational beings are combined, the nonrational form can dominate, though كل له قانتون appears to conflict with that.
rows.anchor: قيل أوقع ما لأنها تقع على أنواع من يعقل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ما diminishes their status, whereas the following description as obedient servants magnifies them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري جاء ب ما تحقيرا لشأنهم وتصغيرا قال له قانتون تعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse escalates from legs to hands to eyes to ears because the later faculties have greater or broader benefits, with hearing highest in importance.
rows.anchor: الترقي كقوله ﴿ ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى الربعي
rows.claim: The source says hearing is paired with reason whereas sight is not, and that a faculty paired with the nobler faculty is itself nobler; this is attributed to Ali ibn Isa al-Rub'i.
rows.anchor: وما قرن بالأشرف كان أشرف وحكى ذلك عن علي بن عيسى الربعي

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو الفتح القشيري
rows.claim: Abu al-Fath al-Qushayri objects that denying the highest attribute first and then lesser ones would intensify the blame, since denying the highest does not entail denying the rest.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو الفتح القشيري فإن قيل قد كان الأولى أن يقدم الوصف الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that the sequence first establishes idols as like their worshippers in being created and subdued, then removes shared attributes from weaker to stronger until all resemblance disappears; this is subtler.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من الآية طريقة أخرى وهي أنه تعالى أثبت أن الأصنام التي تعبدها الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the pronoun in عليه to refer to creation: resurrection by a single cry is easier than developing from sperm through successive stages to adulthood.
rows.anchor: يعود للخلق لأنه يصاح بهم صيحة فيقومون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address يا أيها الساحر may honor Moses as a learned, accomplished man because sorcery was esteemed, or say he defeated them by sorcery; it may also be an attempt to disparage him.
rows.anchor: أي يأيها العالم الكامل وإنما قالوا هذه تعظيما وتوقيرا منهم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional إن, normally associated with uncertainty, taunts the opponents by speaking according to their presumed chance of matching the Qur'an, like a confident challenger.
rows.anchor: جيئ ب إن التي للشك وهو واجب دون اذ التي للوجوب سوقا للكلام على حسب حسبانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من is used for idols, although ما is normal for nonrational things, because the audience treats the idols as deities; the author answers that the wording aims to make the intended target clear to them.
rows.anchor: وكان أصله كما لايخلق لأن ما لمن لايعقل بخلاف من

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh take لعله in its ordinary sense of hope from Moses and Aaron's perspective, since God already knows Pharaoh's outcome; this is better than al-Farra's causal reading.
rows.anchor: اذهبا إلى رجائكما وطمعكما لعله يتذكر عندكما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra interprets لعله as causal, but the author says this takes the wording out of its ordinary function.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن من قول الفراء إنها تعليلة أي يتذكر لما فيه من إخراج اللفظ عن موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some add a causal use to the listed categories, illustrated by the phrase even against yourselves.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم قسما آخر وهو التعليل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh analyzes لولا as a compound of لو and لا, as transmitted by al-Saffar; the author says the sounder analysis is that it is a simple particle.
rows.anchor: مركبة عند سيبويه من لو ولا حكاه الصفار والصحيح أنها بسيطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compounding may change a form or leave it unchanged: لولا stays unchanged, while حبذا becomes a fixed praise formula and هلا loses its interrogative force.
rows.anchor: فمما لا يغير لولا ومما يتغير بالتركيب حبذا صارت للمدح والثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first major use of لولا is to express nonoccurrence because of an existing condition, though some describe it as occurrence because of nonexistence.
rows.anchor: الأول حرف امتناع لوجوب وبعضهم يقول لوجود بالدال

rows.speaker: صاحب رصف المباني
rows.claim: Rasf al-Mabani says the meaning depends on the paired clauses: positive clauses yield nonoccurrence due to existence, while negative clauses yield occurrence due to nonexistence.
rows.anchor: الصحيح إن تفسيرها بحسب الجمل التي تدخل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate after لولا is omitted and supplied by its response; affirmative responses usually take لام, though it can be understood without it.
rows.anchor: ويلزم في خبرها الحذف ويستغنى بجوابها عن الخبر والأكثر في جوابها المثبت اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says Joseph would have desired her but was prevented by seeing his Lord's proof; thus no desire occurred, avoiding the objection that a prophet intended sin.
rows.anchor: لهم بها لكنه امتنع همه بها لوجود رؤية برهان ربه فلم يحصل منه هم البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the response to لولا is negative, Qur'anic usage omits it; this contradicts Ibn Asfur's claim that a negative with ما is better accompanied by لام.
rows.anchor: وأما جوابها إذا كان منفيا فجاء القرآن بالحذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second use of لولا is exhortation or urging, and in this use it takes an imperfect verb.
rows.anchor: الثاني التحضيض فتختص بالمضارع
